en:
...Iwashita's story was over.
Even so, the seventh one never came.
It was already very late.
Waiting any longer {f:would be pointless|would be pointless, wouldn't it}.
{f:I|I} looked around at the faces of the six people who had gathered for me, then bowed deeply.
"Thank you all so much for today.
The seventh person never showed up in the end, but I got to hear some really scary stories."
Having said that much, {f:I|I} glanced over at Kazama.{p}

"...With all this, I think we can put together an interesting school paper.
So I'd like to bring things to a close here..."{p}

Just then, the club room door opened and Hino appeared.
"Hino!"
Hino raised a hand in a light greeting, then sank deep into an empty seat.
He {f:seemed|seemed} really worn out.{p}

"Whew, what a relief.
You're all still here.
Sorry about this, {a}."
{f:I|I} gave a slight bow.
I never thought Hino would be the one to show up{f:.|.}
"Well, see, I couldn't find a seventh person.
I was stuck on what to do.
But I couldn't just leave things like this, right?
Leaving my cute little junior here all alone.
So, since there was no other choice, I figured I'd come myself.
I rushed and got my errands done.
Shindo, Kazama, Iwashita, and everybody else, thanks."
With that, Hino looked at each of our faces in turn.
{f:That's right.|Of course.}
Hino was the only one who {f:knew|knew} everyone here.
Everyone looked at Hino and greeted him in their own way.
"Here. I brought refreshments."
Then Hino carelessly tossed the plastic bag he'd been holding onto the table.{p}

They weren't cans. Every one of them was an unusual mini-size plastic bottle.
I {f:wondered|wondered} what company made them.
"Go on, everybody. Drink whatever you like.
{a}, don't be shy, have whichever one you want."
"Thank you."
There were all kinds of drinks on the table.{p}What should I {f:drink|drink}?
Coffee
Orange juice
Tomato juice
Oolong tea
The last one left

{f:I|I} decided to help myself without holding back.
Everyone took whatever they liked.
From among them, {f:I|I} chose the orange juice.
One hundred percent juice.
I opened the cap and brought it to my mouth.
...Mmm, {f:that's good|delicious}.
Maybe because I'd been so tense, the nicely chilled orange juice felt {f:great|so nice} going down.{p}

...So everybody's done telling their stories, huh?
Did everyone give you their very best ones?
I'm the one who called you all here, after all.
If you didn't tell the scariest stories ever, {a} would laugh at me, and it wouldn't make a good article.
Well, knowing you guys, I'm sure it went fine.
Anyway, I've dug up the best story there is, too, every bit as good as yours.
Get your hopes up and listen.
...You all know Shirai, the science teacher, right?
Still young, but his hair's pure white, so they call him the White-Haired Demon. That Mr. Shirai.
The first-years haven't had Shirai's class yet, so maybe you don't know him, but you've at least seen him, right?
Once you see him, you'll never forget him.{p}

That skinny guy with the skull-like face and sharp, narrow, upturned eyes. The white-haired, middle-aged one.
He's always wearing a lab coat covered in stains.
He's been teaching at this school for about ten years now.
I think you all know this, but there are all kinds of rumors about that teacher.
Well, I can see why the rumors started.
It's not just that he looks shady.
The way he acts is shady too.
I mean, in the science prep room there's a storeroom that not even science club or biology club members are allowed into.
There's a heavy-duty lock on it, and the only one who can go in is Shirai.
Rumor has it even the other teachers can't get in.
They say that once, when somebody tried to go in, he flew into a terrifying rage.
Nobody can even complain.
Except when he's up teaching, Shirai's always shut away in that storeroom, apparently doing some kind of bizarre experiments.
So of course weird rumors are going to start.
But get this. Apparently he's pretty famous in academic circles.
He's published a bunch of really groundbreaking papers, and they say he's a sure bet for a Nobel Prize someday.
So even if a big-shot teacher like that is a little shady, the school has no choice but to look the other way.
Though why such an amazing teacher is teaching at a high school like this one is a mystery.{p}
{a}, you're curious about what Shirai's doing in that storeroom, aren't you?
I'm curious
I'm not curious

Thought so.
Then let me tell you about someone who saw what's inside that storeroom.{p}

The six of you here are all crazy about scary stories, right?
So you must know a lot about the ghost stories surrounding this school, too.
Which means you must know the rumors about Shirai in pretty deep detail.
Including the rumors about the storeroom, of course.
But not one of you knows what's inside that storeroom.
Because nobody's ever seen it.
...But you know what? I found out that secret.
I swear to God, this is true.
I don't lie.
Because the one who went into that storeroom was me.
...Well? Surprised?
Of course, even I couldn't have done it alone.
I could only pull it off because I had a partner, my classmate Yasuo Iwayama.{p}

Shindo, you know Iwayama, right?
Him. You know, that guy.
The one who's good with his hands.
Or you could say he's quick with his hands.
I bet he'd go far if he became a thief... wait, that's a crime, huh.{p}

Shirai's famous for how he guards his keys.
There are three keys just for the storeroom, and the guy's gone and stuck them in a safe, inside a locked cabinet.
Truth is, I'd been working on this plan for about half a year now.
If I uncovered Shirai's secret, that alone would be a guaranteed scoop.
Honestly, I wanted to run it big as a front-page exclusive, not as one piece of some school seven wonders feature like this.
But while I was dragging my feet with one thing and another, this seven wonders project tied to the demolition of the old school building came up, so for me, it's all ending up a bit of a letdown.{p}
Well, this time I'll let my cute little junior have the glory.{p}

So, after half a year, Iwayama and I finally managed to make copies of the storeroom keys.
Don't go calling it a crime, okay?
We put the master keys right back where they belonged, and it's not like we're out to steal anything from the storeroom.
When there's a secret, you want to solve it.
That's the reporter's spirit, right?
...And so, we finally put it into action.
I know Shirai takes one day off a week.
So we took our chance and finally went ahead and broke into the storeroom.
At first, I was worried whether the duplicate keys would fit.
Apparently they were some kind of special keys.
The kind you can't make the normal way.
Still, it worked.
We managed to undo all three locks.{p}

The storeroom door is a heavy iron one.
Even when we opened it slowly and carefully so it wouldn't make a sound, it still let out a harsh, grinding creak of rusty iron.
That sound seemed awfully loud.
Embarrassing to admit, but my heart felt like it was going to burst.
I really felt like a burglar breaking in.{p}
Hey, {a}.{p}What kind of smell do you think it was?
Like rotten eggs
A strong smell of formalin
Like burning corpses
A suffocating, choking smell

Yeah, just like you said.
The place was full of the smell of formalin.{p}

You know what formalin is, right?
That solution they keep animal specimens and stuff in.
It was a harsh stench, like somebody had splashed those jars all over the room.
For a moment, it was like I'd been shot up with anesthetic.
My senses just went haywire.
I got all woozy, my vision blurred, and my head started going foggy.{p}

Thinking it'd be dangerous to stay in there too long, I looked for the light switch.
That's when it happened.{p}

From somewhere, I heard a voice like a baby crying.
The voice seemed to be coming from the back of the storeroom.
Along with the baby's voice, I could also hear the sound of water sloshing.
It gave me a real shock.{p}

And I wondered what on earth was going on.
The room looked like it went pretty far back, but it was pitch-black and I couldn't see a thing.
There seemed to be all kinds of stuff cluttered around, but none of it made any sense.
Walking around carelessly would be dangerous.
If I could just get the light on, I'd be able to see clearly.
I was desperately trying to find the switch.
That's when it happened.
Behind me, I heard the sound of something falling over.{p}

I looked, and there was Iwayama, collapsed on the floor, gasping like he was in pain.
"Hey, Iwayama."
"...Hino. I feel sick.
This room stinks. I can't... take it..."
The formalin stink was so strong that the jerk Iwayama got drunk on it.{p}
Hey, {a}.{p}What do you think I did after that?
Left Iwayama, looked for the switch
Carried Iwayama out of the room

...Right.
Iwayama looked like he was really suffering.
I couldn't just leave him like that.
I hoisted Iwayama onto my back and got out of there.{p}

When I got outside, it hit me all over again how good fresh air could taste.
That's how bad the smell inside was.
Iwayama was puking his guts out.
He must have felt really sick, huh?
I don't even want to imagine what would've happened if I'd just left him there.{p}

So that was the end of it for that day.
We were in no shape to search the storeroom.
So I didn't actually get a clear look at what's inside.
But there's no doubt Shirai's doing some kind of experiment in there.
And he's keeping something alive in there.
A baby crying, and the sound of sloshing water...
That's all I know, but there's definitely something in there.
That's what happened to me exactly one week ago.{p}

...What?
You all look like I let you down.
Relax.
The story's not over yet.
I just figured I'd save the best for last.
Do you get what it means that I snuck in one week ago today?
That's right.
Today is another one of Shirai's days off.
So, to make this story complete, I figured I'd sneak into that storeroom again with Iwayama.
But, see, I can't find Iwayama anywhere.
We promised to go together.
He did look like he didn't want to go, though.
Seems like he ran off.{p}

...But hey, thanks to that, there's even more fun in store.
You know what I'm getting at, right?
The storeroom in the science prep room, which I'm convinced is this school's greatest mystery.
What's in there?
What's really behind the mysterious crying baby and the sound of water?
...Well?
Why don't we all go find out for ourselves, right now?
That's the story I prepared for you.{p}

{a}.
I'm leaving it up to you.
Are we going or not? You decide.{p}Just don't forget that a chance like this will never come again.
Go
Don't go
All right.
{f:Spoken like a real man. |}That's the spirit.

...There's nobody left.
I never knew school could be this quiet.
If a teacher catches us here this late, we'll get chewed out big time.
Everybody, watch your footsteps.
We've still got a ways to go to the science prep room.
Want me to tell you a little about Shirai?{p}
Want to hear it?
I want to hear it
I'd rather hear something else

Apparently Shirai's specialty was bacteriology.
There are countless bacteria in this world.
And there are still loads that haven't been discovered.
And new bacteria keep being born, one after another.
No matter how many new bacteria we discover, we can never keep up.
I don't know exactly what Shirai was researching.
Even I couldn't dig up that much.
But apparently he was obsessed with how bacteria affect living organisms.
...So. I think he's doing that research in that storeroom.
And the thing making that baby-like crying is a new life-form...
No doubt about it.
It's a monster Shirai created.
So if we take a picture of that thing...
We'll be famous overnight.{p}

How about it, {a}?
Just thinking about it gets you excited, right?{p}

...Here we are.
The science prep room.
There's nobody here right now.
Of course there isn't.{p}

Hang on a sec.
I'll get it unlocked.
...Okay, it's open.{p}

All right, we're going in.
The smell's awful, so be careful.{p}

...Geez, where's the light switch?
Usually a light switch is right next to the door.
Hey, {a}.{p}You look for it too.
Look for the switch
Do something else

...Man, it really does stink in here.
I should've brought a flashlight.
Shirai shutting himself up in a place like this? That's just not normal, is it?
{a}, find it yet?
Hurry up.{p}

Crap!
Someone's coming!{p}

Hide!
Hurry, shut the door!
Shhhhhhh!
...Everybody, don't move.{p}

Man, with the door shut the smell's unbelievable.
Just covering our mouths isn't going to cut it.
Everybody okay?
Hey.
Shindo...?{p}

Shindo!
Iwashita?
Kazama?
Hey, everybody...!
{a}!{p}
{f:Is this really|Is this really} the smell of formalin?{p}

The door... the door is opening.
{f:Who's|Who's} that standing there...?
A man with pure white hair... the White-Haired Demon.
...It can't be...?
...I... can't... take... it{f:...|...}...{p}

There was only a dim light bulb, and I couldn't see much of my surroundings.
Was this... was this that storeroom?{p}

It was Hino's voice{f:.|.}
In a corner of my bleary vision, I caught a glimpse of Hino.
Hino stood with his arms crossed, watching {f:me|me} with a satisfied smile.
Next to Hino stood a man in a white coat.
His hair was pure white.
Was that Mr. Shirai{f:?|?}
Mr. Shirai was smiling with satisfaction too.
"Hino. Soon those seven will be your comrades too.
When that happens, be good to them.
Even if they're people you dislike, once they're reborn, you'll all share one fate."
"Of course, sir."
I didn't understand what they were talking about.
Hino came closer to {f:me|me}.
As he did, {f:my|my} vision cleared a little.{p}

It seemed {f:I|I} was in a fairly large tank{f:.|.}
A transparent tank.{p}

Hino folded his arms on the rim of the tank and rested his chin on them.
Then he looked at {f:me|me}.
"...Hey, {a}.
A week ago, I snuck into this storeroom and got caught by Mr. Shirai.
And I was reborn.
...Iwayama, who snuck in with me, ended up dead, though."
With that, he turned his eyes to a corner of the room.{p}
Piled up there were lumps of pale pink flesh.{p}

They were moving, quivering flabbily.
Those lumps of flesh were alive.{p}

When I listened closely, the lumps of flesh were crying.
Crying with that baby's voice...{p}

"Even like that, they're alive.
And now they're my comrades.
The only difference is whether you keep a human shape like this or not."
Then he looked at {f:me|me} once more and laughed.
"...Whether you get to keep the shape you've got now probably depends on you.
If you fuse well, let's make more comrades together.
Hee hee hee..."
Then he turned his eyes the opposite way from the living lumps of flesh.{p}

"Agyii... GYAAAAAAAAHHH!"
To {f:my|my} left, I heard a woman scream.
Even looking was too much trouble.
Still, I reflexively tilted my head a little.{p}

To {f:my|my} left was Iwashita.
Like {f:me|me}, her arms and legs had been taken, and she was soaking in the solution.
Though she was immersed in the lukewarm solution, her skin flaked off in brittle pieces, as if it had lost all its moisture and dried out.
Her muscles sloughed away, her bones dissolved, and she transformed into a lump of flesh.
Even seeing that, {f:I|I} didn't feel so much as fear.
I had a kind of adaptability that let me accept even that as fate.{p}

Once she had become a complete lump of flesh, her seductive flesh-colored body glistening, she let out a newborn baby's first cry.
...She had been reborn{f:.|.}{p}

"Hey there, Iwashita.
Looks like you couldn't fuse properly.
But don't worry.
I'll take care of you from here on.
Kuh hee hee hee..."
Hino put his hand over his mouth as if to hold back his laughter.{p}

Then he looked at {f:me|me} once more, dipped his hand in the solution, and swirled the liquid around, playing with it.
"Hey, {a}.
At a glance, this solution looks like water, right?
But it isn't.
Every kind of bacteria has been put in here on purpose.
It's a culture medium, you could say.
And its main ingredient is a bacterium Mr. Shirai created, with intelligence and abilities more advanced than a human's.
Right now, the world is in an age of explosive population growth.
If it keeps going like this, a food shortage is coming for sure.
But don't worry.
Once you fuse this bacterium with your body, you can live without eating anything.
You can adapt to changes in temperature or environment without any problem at all.
Isn't that wonderful?{p}

...But there's a downside too.
You stop being yourself.
Once this bacterium settles into your body, it completely takes over your will and your body.
All your memories and feelings up to now disappear.
That's the only shame of it.
I'm going to end up like that soon, too.
In about ten days, I'll be completely reborn as a new life-form.
...I'll stop being me.
That's so frustrating.
And I hate it.{p}

Hey, {a}.
Do you know how I picked the people for this group?
I gathered the ones I can't stand.
People whose faces I don't like, people whose personalities I don't like, people who piss me off just looking at them, people I hate for no reason I can name.
That's who I gathered.
{a}. You know, I hated you.
So I wanted to make you taste the same fate as me.{p}

...Too bad, huh.
Oh, {a}.
The skin on your face is peeling off.
You're just like Iwashita.
You're turning into nothing but a lump of flesh.
Serves you right.
...What's wrong, {a}?
You're starting to melt.
Hey, come on.
Can you hear me?
If you can hear me, try answering.{p}

Hyahahaha... of course you can't answer.
Your voice already sounds like a baby's.
I'll take care of you.
I fused successfully.
And you failed.
And as a result, you turned into a monstrous lump of flesh.
So I'll gladly take care of you.
...Are you not conscious anymore, {a}?"{p}

{f:I|I} decided to help myself without holding back.
Everyone took whatever they liked.
{f:I|I} chose the coffee.
Iced coffee, of course, chilled ice-cold{f:.|.}
I twisted off the cap and raised it to my mouth.
...Mmm, {f:good stuff|delicious}.
I drank it in one go, so I got a sharp brain freeze.
After the muggy heat and the tension of the scary stories, the nicely chilled iced coffee was a real refresher{f:.|.}{p}

{f:I|I} decided to help myself without holding back.
Everyone took whatever they liked.
{f:I|I} chose the oolong tea.
{f:I'm|I'm} not fond of sweet things, so I can't drink much juice, even if it's a hundred percent fruit juice.
When you're thirsty, nothing beats tea{f:.|.}
What I'd really like is hot Japanese green tea{f:, but|, but} since Hino was treating us, I couldn't be picky.
There are many different kinds of oolong tea.
This one was pu-erh tea, which is rare in Japan.
It was a pretty crimson color you'd never expect from oolong.
{f:I|I} drank the pu-erh tea in one go.
...Mmm, {f:good stuff|delicious}.
It had a bit of a peculiar aftertaste{f:, but|, but} it was pretty good{f:.|.}
I'd ask Hino later who made this tea.
After all the scary stories so far, my mood had turned somehow gloomy, and I'd felt as if I were in another world.
{f:But|But} thanks to this cold oolong tea, I was pulled back to reality a little{f:.|.}{p}

Since {f:I|I} was the one running this meeting, I decided to take whatever was left over.
What was left was... of all things, a red-bean soup drink.
"..."
{f:I|I} was at a loss for words.
Had Hino seriously chosen and bought something like this{f:?|?}
Maybe he picked it as a joke.
Seeing {f:me|me} looking so troubled, Hino said,
"Oh, {a}!
Lucky you!
I love red-bean soup drinks.
Especially the ice-cold ones.
I grabbed one out of habit..."
...I see, so Hino had chosen it in earnest{f:.|.}
But do they even sell cold red-bean soup drinks?
{f:I|I} opened the cap and bravely took a drink.
...Oh, it's actually pretty good!
Huh, that's a new discovery{f:.|.}
{f:I|I} drank it with a big smile.{p}

Don't lie to me.
With your eyes shining like that, you can't tell me you're 'not curious.'
Come on, be honest.{p}You really are curious about what Shirai's doing, aren't you?
Actually, I am
I'm really not

Huh. Is that so?
Maybe you're not cut out for the newspaper club, huh?{p}
If you're not out to grab a scoop, there's no way you can do good work.{p}

Hino's angry face swam and warped.
Huh...?
Something was wrong{f:.|.}
{f:I|I} hurriedly tried to stand up.
But there was no strength in my legs.
I collapsed right onto the floor.
I thought I saw someone bending down over me, filling my blurring vision.{p}

.........................................
............My head hurt.
It was pounding.
Like I had an oil drum over my head and people were banging on it from all around.{p}

{f:I|I} opened my eyes.
...Wait, this was the newspaper club room{f:, wasn't it|, wasn't it}?
Why was I sleeping in a place like {f:this|this}?
In my foggy head, my memories gradually came back.
...{f:Right|Right}, while I was talking with Hino, I suddenly got dizzy and...
Did {f:I|I} collapse{f:?|?}
Just then, I saw something move at the edge of my vision.{p}

When I looked that way, something was slithering out through the gap in the door.
{f:What|What} was that just now?
The hand I put down to push myself up slid out from under me.
"{f:Whoa|Eek}!"
{f:I|I} fell to the floor again.
{f:What|What} was this dark liquid?
Now that I thought about it, this smell...
{f:I|I} carefully, slowly got up.{p}

{f:I|I} jumped in spite of myself.
Someone was shouting outside the door.
"What happened?
What was that scream just now?!"
"Open up! Open this door!"
......It was the teachers{f:.|.}{p}

Only then did {f:I|I} finally realize.
The door was locked from the inside.{p}

That's right.
Do you know what rotten eggs smell like?
It's a smell that makes you feel like gas is building up in your lungs just from one sniff. It gives you goosebumps.
It made me feel sick right away.
I staggered and leaned against the wall.
That's when I sensed something in the darkness.{p}

I sensed something creeping up on us.
And with it, the smell got stronger.
I couldn't tell what it was that was coming closer.
But this stench was coming from it.
I held my breath as best I could and tried to slip away quietly.
If I breathed, I'd be taking that smell into my body, and I didn't want to make noise and tell it where I was, either.
But it was no use.
It was walking straight toward us.
I could feel it looking at us.
It could see us, even in pitch darkness.
And then, finally.
Right beside me, I heard Iwayama scream.
Then came a sound like something being crushed.
It's embarrassing to admit, but I think my legs gave out.
I slid down to the floor and couldn't move after that...{p}

"...You want to know?"
...I caught a whiff of something rank, like raw meat.
Where was it coming {f:from|from}?
"If you want to know, I'll tell you."{p}

Hino came closer to {f:me|me}.
Was it just my imagination{f:?|?}
The smell seemed to be getting stronger...
A smell like something rotting, one that stung my eyes.
"Do I smell that bad?"
Before I knew it, Hino was standing right in front of me.
I was right, this smell was coming from Hino!
{f:I|I} couldn't say a word anymore, and Hino grinned at me.
"Iwayama got eaten......by me."{p}
{f:What did you say|Whaaat}★{p}

What did this person just {f:say|say}?
"H-Hino... c-cut it out with the jokes, please."
My voice shook so badly it was pathetic, even to me.
But Hino's expression didn't change.
"Hino? Oh, I ate him too.
That's right, me."{p}

Hino's face split open vertically.
From the split peeked rows upon rows of sharp fangs.
Someone screamed.
The next moment, the world around {f:me|me} vanished.{p}

Don't talk nonsense.
Have you ever smelled a dead body?
I haven't.
So even if I smelled one, I wouldn't know.
I figure it'd be a nasty smell, though.
What I smelled was formalin.{p}

That's right.
A rank smell, like raw meat, or like a wild animal.
And it came drifting in on a lukewarm breeze.
It was way beyond just disgusting.
Iwayama and I looked at each other and tried to go back the way we came.
The very next moment, an arm reached out of the darkness and grabbed Iwayama!
That thick arm, covered in bristly hair, dragged Iwayama in.
And then.
Iwayama screamed!
I got scared and ran without even looking back.
In the darkness I tripped and banged into things all over, but I couldn't care less about that.{p}

Hino looked down and fell silent.
"U-Um... is that the end?"
{f:I|I} asked without thinking.
With an ending {f:that|that} abrupt, anyone would want to know{f:.|.}
Hino raised his face.
"I left him to die.
To make up for it, I swore an oath."
Hino looked at {f:me|me} with a stern expression.
"That I'd take down the monster that ate him with my own hands!"{p}
At some point, he had a knife in his hand.{p}
His eyes were fixed on.......................{f:me|me}!{p}

Hino came at me with blazing eyes.
"No matter what you disguise yourself as, I can tell.
You're the one who ate Iwayama. It's you!"
What had gotten into him?
He was like a completely different person from the usual Hino, who always looked out for everyone.
To think he had delusions like this!{p}

"Die, {a}!"
I desperately dodged the knife as it thrust at me.
Hino {f:meant it|meant it}!{p}What should I do?
Run away
Fight back

All I could do was run!
{f:I|I} ran for the door.
Just a little more and I'd have my hand on the doorknob!
I reached out desperately.{p}
At that moment, something hot and heavy slammed into my back.{p}

As if all my strength were draining out from there, {f:I|I} sank limply to the floor.
Just like a balloon with a hole in it.
When I reached around to my back, I felt something slick.
......Blood?{p}

The people looking down at me let out small screams.
What {f:was|was} wrong?
Hurry, stop Hino and call a teacher{f:, someone|, someone}...
{f:I|I} tried to say that, and raised my hand toward the voices.{p}

On that hand was a cloudy white liquid.
...What {f:was|was} this?
If it had been stained red with blood, that would be one thing, but why was it like this...?
"This one's blood... why is it white?"
I heard someone's voice.
White?
{f:White blood?|White blood?}{p}

That's crazy...
